title: Support for AI Catalog and MCP Server Card
summary: MCP clients can now find and configure the Resend MCP server from a single URL.
body_markdown:
Adding an MCP server to a client usually means digging through docs for the right endpoint, transport, and auth setup. Resend now publishes an **AI Catalog** and an **MCP Server Card** , so supporting clients can discover the Resend MCP server from just a URL.


## How discovery works


Both files are public, static JSON documents any client can read before connecting:


- **AI Catalog** at` resend.com/.well-known/ai-catalog.json` lists the AI artifacts Resend offers, including the remote MCP server.
- **MCP Server Card** at` mcp.resend.com/mcp/server-card` describes the server's name, Streamable HTTP endpoint, and supported protocol versions.


Give a client that supports these discovery methods` resend.com` , and it reads the AI Catalog, follows the entry to the Server Card, and connects. You still sign in with OAuth, or pass a Resend API key as a Bearer token for headless setups.


## Built on open standards


The[AI Catalog](https://ai-catalog.io/) format is maintained by the Agent Card Working Group under the Linux Foundation. MCP Server Cards are defined in[SEP-2127](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/2127-mcp-server-cards) , an official MCP extension.


## Get started


If your client supports Server Card discovery, add` resend.com` as an MCP server and follow the sign-in prompt. For every other client, the server is hosted at` https://mcp.resend.com/mcp` .


For more installation options, see the[MCP server documentation](https://resend.com/docs/mcp-server) .
